title: Offline Full-Text Index Engine Architecture
subtitle: Analysis of data structure selection achieving 85,000 docs/sec write throughput and 4.2 ms P99 query latency.
author: Core Search Architecture Committee

summary.claim: Because traditional B+ Tree indexing incurred excessive random I/O and page splits during 100,000,000 offline document ingestion, throughput degraded to 12,000 docs/sec. Therefore, the architecture migrated to LSM-Tree with tiered MemTable and SSTable structures. Because Posting Lists comprised over 60% of storage, Delta Varint was replaced with Roaring Bitmap for chunked compression and SIMD bitwise logic. This refactoring reduced index storage from 48 GB to 14.4 GB (-70.0%), increased write throughput to 85,000 docs/sec (+608.3%), and cut P99 latency from 38.6 ms to 4.2 ms (-89.1%).
takeaways: Because LSM-Tree converts random I/O into sequential disk writes, ingestion throughput increased from 12,000 to 85,000 docs/sec.
Because Roaring Bitmap uses 16-bit containers and SIMD bitwise AND, compression ratio improved by 70.0%, shrinking storage from 48 GB to 14.4 GB.
Because Memory-mapped I/O with 64-byte cache line alignment eliminates copy overhead, P99 query latency dropped from 38.6 ms to 4.2 ms.
Because a Bloom Filter with 10 hash functions caps the false positive rate at 1%, 99% of unnecessary SSTable disk reads were avoided.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Background & Offline Index Bottlenecks
chapters.claim: Because the system must build full-text indexes for 100,000,000 documents (120 GB raw text) within a 4-hour batch window, the existing B+ Tree architecture triggers severe page splits and random I/O, capping write throughput at 12,000 docs/sec.
paragraphs: The legacy architecture used a B+ Tree to manage inverted indexes. When processing 100,000,000 documents (1.2 KB average size, total 120 GB), index nodes suffered frequent random insertions and page splits across 4 KB pages. Measurements indicate that after B+ Tree depth reached 5 levels, disk Read-Before-Write overhead consumed 68% of I/O time. Single-node ingestion throughput dropped precipitously from 45,000 docs/sec to 12,000 docs/sec, extending total index construction time for 120 GB data to 2.3 hours against a 4-hour batch limit.

On the query side, legacy SkipList inverted lists lacked memory alignment. A multi-term intersection query required traversing DocID arrays exceeding 500,000 elements. Pointer chasing induced an L3 Cache Miss Rate of 42.1%, driving P99 query latency to 38.6 ms. Under a modest 1,000 QPS concurrent load, CPU core utilization hit a saturation ceiling of 94.2%.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Architecture Selection & LSM-Tree / Roaring Bitmap Refactoring
chapters.claim: Because LSM-Tree transforms random writes into sequential 64 MB WAL and MemTable buffers, coupled with Roaring Bitmap 16-bit container chunking and SIMD bitwise processing, the system completely resolves disk I/O bottlenecks and memory cache misalignment.
paragraphs: Phase one of refactoring completely replaced the B+ Tree with an LSM-Tree write engine. Incoming documents write sequentially to a 64 MB Write-Ahead Log (WAL) before in-memory sorting inside a SkipList MemTable. Upon reaching 64 MB, the MemTable freezes and flushes sequentially to L0 SSTable files at 128 MB/s. Empirical data confirms this design reduced random disk write ratio from 84.5% to 0.0%, surging write throughput to 85,000 docs/sec—a 608.3% increase.

Phase two redesigned the Posting List compression algorithm, replacing Delta Varint with Roaring Bitmaps. Roaring Bitmap splits 32-bit DocIDs into upper 16-bit container keys and lower 16-bit values. Containers holding fewer than 4,096 elements use Array Containers; those above 4,096 use 8 KB Bitmap Containers, while contiguous runs convert to RLE Containers. Executing bitwise AND with AVX-512 SIMD processes 256 bits per cycle, accelerating list intersection by 4.8x and compressing overall index size from 48 GB to 14.4 GB (-70.0%).

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Benchmark Data & Performance Evaluation
chapters.claim: In rigorous benchmark tests across 100,000,000 real-world documents, the refactored solution demonstrated quantifiable superiority across write throughput, P99 query latency, and memory footprint, fully satisfying production SLA requirements.
paragraphs: To validate performance, the team conducted 3 runs of benchmark tests on 100,000,000 documents (120 GB total) using an 8-core CPU, 32 GB RAM, and NVMe SSD setup. Ingestion throughput jumped from 12,000 docs/sec under the legacy B+ Tree to 85,000 docs/sec (+608.3%), cutting total index build time for 120 GB from 2.3 hours down to 19.6 minutes.

On the query engine side, leveraging Memory-mapped I/O (mmap) with 64-byte Cache Line alignment and Roaring Bitmap SIMD instructions dropped P99 query latency from 38.6 ms to 4.2 ms (-89.1%). Additionally, LSM-Tree compaction paired with a 10-hash Bloom Filter (1.0% false positive rate) eliminated 99.0% of invalid disk seeks. Total index storage shrank from 48 GB to 14.4 GB (-70.0%), and memory cache footprint decreased from 12.8 GB to 3.8 GB (-70.3%).

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Architecture Conclusion & Future Roadmap
chapters.claim: Because the LSM-Tree and Roaring Bitmap architecture successfully overcame I/O and memory bottlenecks in offline indexing, the system now possesses a foundation to support 1,000,000,000 documents, paving the way for GPU vector acceleration and dynamic tiering.
paragraphs: This architectural refactoring proves that in large-scale offline full-text search, append-only LSM-Tree combined with vector-friendly Roaring Bitmap significantly outperforms traditional B+ Trees. Reducing 120 GB index build time to 19.6 minutes reduces batch maintenance window utilization to just 8.2%, relieving scheduler bottlenecks during data scaling.

Future roadmap initiatives focus on two areas: First, integrating hybrid AVX-512 and GPU CUDA kernels in Q1 2027 to further optimize Roaring Bitmap multi-term AND/OR evaluation. Second, introducing dynamic hot-cold tiering to archive index data older than 30 days to remote NVMe-oF storage, guaranteeing local SSD footprint remains below 20.0 GB.
